ov: A family of 385 species of tiny, mouse-like mammals that are not rodents at all; their closest relatives are hedgehogs and moles. Shrews have a very high metabolism and must eat almost constantly, and some species are venomous or use echolocation.
len: 3.5 cm (Etruscan shrew) to about 15 cm (Asian house shrew)
rg: Almost worldwide, except New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand and most of South America (a few now live in the northern Andes).
df: Insects, worms, seeds and nuts from leaf litter; captives eat half to twice their body weight a day.

cf.tip: A shrew has sharp, spiky teeth and a longer nose; a mouse is a rodent with gnawing front teeth.

fx: The Etruscan shrew, at about 1.8 g, is the smallest known land mammal.
Young shrews "caravan" behind their mother, each gripping the fur of the one in front.
